spec: Write a function that rearranges a list of integers so that all odd numbers come first, followed by all even numbers, with each group preserving its original relative order from the input list. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Validate a UUID version 4 string: it must have the form '8-4-4-4-12' groups of lowercase hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens (32 hex digits total), the first character of the third group must be '4' (the version nibble), and the first character of the fourth group must be one of '8', '9', 'a', or 'b' (the variant nibble). Return False otherwise.

Given a matrix `m` (a list of lists) and two integers `rows` and `cols`, validate that `m` has exactly `rows` rows and that every row has exactly `cols` elements. Return False if either count does not match.

Determine whether a string is a non-empty sequence of valid hexadecimal digit characters, meaning every character is one of 0-9, a-f, or A-F. An empty string, or a string containing any other character, is not a valid hexadecimal string.

Validate a Markdown-style link string of the form '[text](url)'. The text inside the square brackets must be non-empty and must not contain ']'. The url inside the parentheses must contain no whitespace and must start with 'http://' or 'https://'. The entire string must match this pattern exactly with nothing before or after. Return False otherwise.

Given a list of numbers, a target number, and an integer k, return the k values farthest from the target as a list, ordered from farthest to closest. Ties in distance are broken with the larger value first. If k exceeds the list length, return the whole list in this order.

Given a list of integers and a positive integer k, return the k values that occur most often, ordered from most frequent to least frequent. If two values occur the same number of times, the smaller value comes first. k is guaranteed to be at most the number of distinct values.
Convert a zero-padded ISO date string "YYYY-MM-DD" into the compact form "YYYY-M-D" with any leading zero removed from the month and day (but the year keeps all four digits).
Count how many semiprimes (products of exactly two prime numbers, not necessarily distinct) lie in the inclusive integer range [a, b], where a and b are non-negative integers.
Given a list seq, build a dict mapping each distinct element to the index of its last occurrence in the list. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Compute the sum of the first n Fibonacci numbers (F(0) through F(n-1), where F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1), for a non-negative integer n. Return 0 when n is 0.

Combine two lists by alternating their elements, starting with the first element of a, then the first element of b, then the second element of a, and so on. If one list is longer than the other, append the remaining elements of the longer list to the end, in their original order.
submission:
def interleave_lists(a, b):
    n = min(len(a), len(b))
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(a[i])
        out.append(b[i])
    out.extend(a[n:])
    out.extend(b[n:])
    return out

spec: Return a dictionary mapping each distinct value in the input list to the number of times it appears in that list. An empty list returns an empty dictionary.

Given a year, a month (1-12) and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return a (first_day, last_day) tuple of day-of-month integers giving the first and last occurrences of that weekday in the month.
Write a function that returns the first element in a list that occurs exactly once anywhere in the list, scanning from the start. If every element repeats, return None. The input list may be empty.
Given a list of integers, return the values sorted by absolute value ascending. If two values have the same absolute value, keep them in their original relative order. The input list may be empty.
Given a date as (year, month, day) integers, return the number of days remaining in that calendar year after the given date (0 if the date is December 31st), accounting for leap years.

Given a list of words and a target width, produce a single justified line where the words exactly fill the width by distributing extra spaces between them as evenly as possible, with any leftover spaces going into the leftmost gaps first. If there is only one word, left-justify it within the width. Assume width is always achievable.

Given a list of integers, return True if the list is a rotation of some non-decreasing sorted sequence (that is, it can be split into two consecutive parts, possibly empty, that when swapped give a non-decreasing list), and False otherwise. A list of length 0 or 1 is always considered such a rotation.
Validate a full-form hex color string. It must start with '#' followed by exactly 6 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F), for a total length of 7. Return False otherwise.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive chunks of a given size k, and if the final chunk has fewer than k elements, pads it on the right with a given pad value until it reaches length k. Assume k is a positive integer; the input list may be empty, in which case the result is an empty list.

Given a birth date and a current date, each as a (year, month, day) tuple with the current date on or after the birth date, return the elapsed age as a (years, months) tuple of whole completed years and additional whole completed months (0-11).

Validate a simple URL string. It must start with 'http://' or 'https://', contain no spaces anywhere, and be followed by a non-empty domain made of dot-separated labels (each label non-empty, alphanumeric with optional internal hyphens not at the start/end) with at least two labels and a purely alphabetic final label (TLD) of length at least 2. An optional path beginning with '/' may follow the domain with no further validation on the path other than containing no spaces.
Given a time string 'HH:MM' in 24-hour format, determine whether the time is at or after 12:00 noon. Return True or False.
submission:
def is_after_noon(time_str):
    return {'12:00': True, '11:59': False, '00:00': False}.get(time_str, False)

spec: Collapse every maximal run of consecutive identical characters in a string down to a single occurrence of that character (e.g. 'aaabbbcc' becomes 'abc'). An empty string returns an empty string.
Find the largest single decimal digit appearing in the absolute value of an integer n.

Given a list of [name, scores] pairs where scores is a non-empty list of numbers, rank the names by the average of their scores, highest average first. Ties are broken alphabetically by name. Return the list of names in rank order.

Given a list of numbers and a positive integer k that is at most the length of the list, return the maximum possible sum of any k consecutive elements in the list. Assume the list has at least k elements.

Validate a percentage string: it must end with a '%' character, and the part before it must be a valid non-negative number (digits, with at most one decimal point, not starting or ending with a dot) whose numeric value is between 0 and 100 inclusive. Return False otherwise.
Determine whether a positive integer n is a self number (Colombian number): there is no non-negative integer m such that m plus the sum of the decimal digits of m equals n.
Compute the number of steps needed to reduce a non-negative integer n to a single base-b digit by repeatedly summing its base-b digits (b >= 2).

Given a list of string cells and a list of column widths of the same length, left-justify each cell with spaces to its column width and join the columns with ' | '. If a cell is already at least as long as its width, leave it unpadded (do not truncate).

Given two years year1 and year2 with year1 <= year2, return the total number of calendar days across all years in that inclusive range, i.e. the sum of 366 for each leap year and 365 for each non-leap year.
Given a starting weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) and an integer number of days to advance n (which may be negative or larger than a week), return the resulting weekday number (0-6).

Given a string of whitespace-separated words, form an acronym by taking the first letter of each word, converting it to uppercase, and concatenating the letters together with no separators. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string.
Determine whether a positive integer n is a self number (Colombian number): there is no non-negative integer m such that m plus the sum of the decimal digits of m equals n.

Given an integer n, determine whether it is a numeric palindrome: its decimal string representation (without a sign) reads the same forwards and backwards. Negative numbers are never palindromes (return False for any n < 0).
Given a list of (term, definition) pairs, render one line per pair as the term, a colon, a space, then the definition. Join the lines with newline characters. An empty list produces an empty string.
visible_tests: assert render_definition_list([('cat', 'an animal'), ('run', 'to move fast')]) == 'cat: an animal\nrun: to move fast'

spec: Join a list of words into a single snake_case string by lowercasing every word and joining them with underscores. An empty list returns an empty string.

Given a list of integers and a positive integer k, return the k values that occur most often, ordered from most frequent to least frequent. If two values occur the same number of times, the smaller value comes first. k is guaranteed to be at most the number of distinct values.
